flashcard_questions.a: New, original data collected first-hand by the researcher.
Existing data collected by someone else and reused for a new purpose.
Descriptive data that records opinions and feelings in words.
Numerical data that can be measured and counted as statistics.

flashcard_questions.q: Which primary research method brings a small target-audience group together to discuss ideas?
Which primary research method uses one-to-one questioning of a participant?

flashcard_questions.a: An interview that uses a set list of questions.

flashcard_questions.q: Why can online surveys reach many people cheaply?
flashcard_questions.a: They are distributed digitally through websites, email or social media.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the main weakness of an online survey?
flashcard_questions.a: Response rates can be low and follow-up questions are difficult.

flashcard_questions.q: Which secondary source is described as the most authoritative?
Why must internet sources be evaluated critically?
flashcard_questions.a: Online sources vary widely in reliability.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the main age-related weakness of secondary research data?
flashcard_questions.a: The data may be out of date.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is primary research data more relevant than secondary data?
flashcard_questions.a: It is collected specifically for your project and audience.

notes: 13 cards: 5 term-to-definition, 2 method-to-description, 3 weakness cards, 3 causal. Qualitative and quantitative definitions were rewritten without example lists so the answers are not enumerations.
